risks.note: BRSR material issue 1 (Risk, negative implications): physical risk to the workforce in manufacturing operations and frontline distribution teams; inadequate OHS training could cause incidents, accidents and even fatalities, with indirect risk of workplace closures, higher legal and compliance costs, stakeholder scrutiny, lower morale and brand damage. Mitigated by a Health & Safety policy, SOPs, incident investigation, periodic review and a Central Safety Committee plus plant-level committees reviewing monthly data; GCPL cites a consistent record of zero fatalities across offices and plants.

BRSR material issue 2 (Risk, negative implications): an evolving regulatory landscape and changing guidelines on the composition of ingredients and raw materials pose a risk of disruption to operations. Mitigated through quality testing SOPs for all products, raw-material testing procedures and skill-development training.
risks.risk: Product safety and quality / evolving ingredient regulation

risks.note: BRSR material issue 3 (Risk, negative implications): greenwashing or ethically and factually incorrect marketing practices and claims pose reputational risk. Mitigated by the code of conduct, whistle blower, anti-sexual harassment, human rights and health & safety policies, and a Responsible Marketing, Advertising and Sales Policy aligned to local and international standards.
risks.risk: Business ethics and ethical marketing (greenwashing / labelling)

risks.note: BRSR material issue 4 (Risk, negative implications): the need to meet all reporting and transparency requirements of market regulators and to voluntarily disclose against international ESG frameworks. GCPL reports under BRSR in India plus CDP, GRI and Integrated Reporting <IR>.

BRSR material issue 6 (Risk, negative implications): procurement from diverse suppliers carries ESG compliance risk for critical suppliers and unethical sourcing practices. Under the Policy for Responsible Supply, 49% of suppliers by procurement spend were evaluated for ESG performance in FY25-26.

BRSR material issue 5, flagged as an Opportunity: stricter regulation on plastic use, waste generation, disposal and EPR across geographies such as India and Africa is accelerating the transition to sustainable packaging; most GCPL products involve plastic packaging, so plastic packaging intensity and EPR cost are a structural exposure being managed rather than an unaddressed risk.
risks.risk: Regulatory pressure on plastic packaging and Extended Producer Responsibility
